items.before: I reviewed the workspace tooling diff (3c28ff5a~1..HEAD) across tim exec (stack, stack-lease, stack-refresh, stack-fingerprints, docker-daemon), tim build gate, tim backlog split, split-off and themes, tim distil, and the increment-build-loop workflow. The backlog split-off, relink, distil and x-refresh-with code is sound and well tested. The main defect: when Docker Desktop has quit, tim now starts it again inside every `docker ps`, and the gate then treats the run's own down stack as one it started itself. It releases that stack after the e2e rungs, which takes it down and deletes the run's lease. So the new recover-and-re-lease path almost never runs. A second risk: the new rollback step in the failed-attempt handler soft-resets every unpushed commit in each repo, not just the failed attempt's. Neither lets wrong code land green; both affect lease safety and keeping the branch's history intact.
items.after:

- tim distil
- the increment-build-loop workflow

- When Docker Desktop has quit, tim now starts it again inside every `docker ps`.
- The gate then treats the run's own down stack as one it started itself.

items.before:
Animals backend templates package (#106, 9 commits merged cleanly into the combined branch). Per-user scoping holds. Every read and write goes through findByIdAndOwnerId or findAllByOwnerId, and another user's template answers 404. No path writes a template to the outbox, to SNS or to PIMS: it uses its own notification_templates collection with no Mongo event listeners or change streams. Six findings, none critical:

items.id: templates area: Workspace tooling changed on laptop 2
items.before:
The five laptop-2 commits make long gates work, mostly correctly: gate-wait waits in slices, results are written atomically, the parallelRepos worker pool is right, and stackAfterLocal holds the lease and stack refresh until layer one finishes. Three real risks remain, all in waiting on a long gate.
1. A result file carries nothing that says which gate run wrote it, and two gates for the same holder are not stopped from running at once. A gate the agent gave up on keeps running, and its result can land in the next gate's file and be read as that gate's verdict, possibly green on untested code.
2. gate-wait cannot tell a crashed gate from a slow one. A gate killed by memory pressure or a tool kill costs up to about 3h10m of waiting before anyone calls it red.
3. The lease teardown found this morning (a gate that finds the run's stack down restarts it under the run's own holder, then releases it at the end) is not fixed by these commits. stackAfterLocal makes the window for it bigger.
Also lower: 664beddd stopped writing (or clearing) a result when argument checks or workspace lookup fail, and the help, plain-text report and docs still say repos run at the same time and the stack gets ready during layer one. Test quality is mostly in line with tim/CLAUDE.md (input and output, no spies), but nothing tests a dead or overlapping gate, a cap between 1 and N, or the refresh path with a reused lease.
items.after:

- the parallelRepos worker pool is right
- stackAfterLocal holds the lease and stack refresh until layer one finishes

Three real risks remain, all in waiting on a long gate.

1. A result file carries nothing that says which gate run wrote it.

- Two gates for the same holder are not stopped from running at once.
- A gate the agent gave up on keeps running.
- Its result can land in the next gate's file and be read as that gate's verdict, possibly green on untested code.

2. gate-wait cannot tell a crashed gate from a slow one.

- A gate killed by memory pressure or a tool kill costs up to about 3h10m of waiting before anyone calls it red.

3. These commits do not fix the lease teardown found this morning.

- In that teardown, a gate that finds the run's stack down restarts it under the run's own holder, then releases it at the end.
- stackAfterLocal makes the window for it bigger.

Also lower:

- The help, plain-text report and docs still say repos run at the same time and the stack gets ready during layer one.

Test quality is mostly in line with tim/CLAUDE.md (input and output, no spies).

But nothing tests:

items.id: templates area: Frontend shared code changed by templates
items.before:
I reviewed the shared code the templates merge changed in the animals, INS and plants frontends. Template mode cannot leak into a real notification. The template wrapper (AsyncLocalStorage) runs only inside the generated /templates handlers. The records port, path builders, journeyStrip, save-actions and base() only switch inside that wrapper. The notification entry guard only matches /notifications/ paths. A template id never joins the known-journeys cookie, and the template records port is scoped to the owner and refuses create, list, finalise, amend, copy and softDelete. Review submit in template mode short-circuits to saveTemplate, and Use template creates its notification outside template mode.

I found 7 real problems:
1. (High) The INS "Add a new address" round trip from a template's party picker strands the user on a 404 and loses the address.
2. (Medium) A new INS CSP form-action setting defaults to localhost and is missing from the cdp-app-config checkout. On CDP, the type question's hand-over can be blocked when it has to bounce through Defra ID sign-in.
3. (Medium) The plants Templates nav link defaults to http://localhost:3000 and is not set in the cdp-app-config checkout.
4. (Medium) A GET on /start creates a draft in animals and plants. That goes against the "every state change is a form post" ruling, and prefetch or cross-site links create stray drafts.
5. (Low) Choosing Germinal products in template creation silently drops the user back on Manage templates.
6. (Low) Lighthouse never audits a template-mode page.
7. (Low) Template saves drop the concurrency token, so the last save wins without warning.

Note: the cdp-app-config checkout used for findings 2 and 3 was last committed on 28 Sep, so check the live repo before acting on those two.

It does not bypass the proxy. With HTTP_PROXY set, backend calls use built-in fetch and the global proxy agent, as before. That also means the 2 second bound never applies in CDP, and the retry fires only if the socket to the proxy itself fails. A backend the proxy cannot reach comes back as a 5xx or a tunnelling error, and neither is retried.

In CDP the change is effectively dead code. It also puts CDP on a different fetch and FormData path from every test environment (finding rank 5).

Retry safety. Connect timeout and connection refused happen before any bytes are sent, so a create, submit or upload cannot be duplicated. ETIMEDOUT is the exception (finding rank 25).
